Subject: Probe: log filtering & trace-id policy confirmation

Hi Aileen — thanks again for the demo earlier. Quick recap + asks so we can scope the sanitization work and timeline: 

Summary from call:
- PulseCare needs request/response logging for troubleshooting production incidents, but cannot retain any direct PII in plain text.
- Trace IDs are used by your SREs for session stitching; you want a way to keep trace linkage for debugging without exposing raw IDs to downstream logs.
- Retention target: 30 days for sanitized logs; longer retention for aggregated metrics is fine.

Action items / questions for confirmation:
1) Can you confirm the exact fields you consider PII (we saw patient_name, email, ssn in the PIIscope doc — is that complete?)
2) For trace IDs, is deterministic pseudonymization (hashing with tenant salt) acceptable, or do you require irreversible truncation/mapping?
3) Do you need full request/response bodies retained in any environment (staging vs prod)?
4) Are there regulatory export constraints (e.g., EU residency) for subsets of logs?

Attached: redwood-log-sanitization-checklist.pdf — quick mapping of options (masking, hashing, tokenization) and the tradeoffs.

Proposed next step: if you confirm the PII list and trace-ID policy, we can produce a short implementation plan (estimated 2 sprints) + cost delta.

Thanks — I’ll loop in Ben & Karthik for the technical details once you confirm.

Best,
Monica Patel
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Thanks, Monica — great write-up. Confirming from our side:

- PIIs: yes — patient_full_name, patient_email, patient_dob, ssn, and any insurance identifiers (plan_id) must be removed or tokenized before long-term storage. I attached an updated scoping doc.
- Trace IDs: we prefer pseudonymization that preserves one-to-one mapping within our tenant (deterministic hash salted per-tenant) so SREs can stitch sessions but raw IDs are not reversible by default.
- Environments: staging may contain synthetic data only; production is the only environment requiring the full implementation.
- Residency: all logs for EU customers must remain in eu-central region; PulseCare is US-based so current scope is US only, but we can revisit if we expand.

One additional ask: can Redwood provide us a safe-preview mechanism (preview logs with masked values) so our security team can validate that no PII leaks before we enable retention?

I attached PulseCare_PIIscope_v2.pdf. Happy to jump on a tech sync next week.

—Aileen
Director of Engineering, PulseCare

Aileen — thanks for the clarifications. Quick responses and an option matrix so we can align on cost and SLO impact: 

Options for PII handling (short):
- Field redaction (mask at ingest): lowest storage risk, minimal CPU overhead, retains log shape but removes sensitive substrings.
- Tokenization (vault mapping): allows reversible lookup under strict access controls; higher operational overhead.
- Full discard of bodies containing PII: cheapest but may impact debugging fidelity.

Trace-ID approaches:
- Deterministic salted hash per-tenant: meets your ask; cost: small CPU hit at ingest and minimal storage increase for mapping metadata.
- One-way truncation + internal mapping table: still feasible but requires careful mapping lifecycle (rotation/handoff).

Safe-preview: we can provide a quarantine preview endpoint (read-only) that returns redacted samples for validation. This would be a time-limited view, accessible to your security team.

Estimate: implementing deterministic hashing + field-level redaction in prod ~2-3 weeks of engineering + 1 week QA; cost impact estimate attached (pc-cost-estimate-sanitization.xlsx).

If that timeline works, we’ll produce an SOW and run a 2-week pilot on a subset of traffic.

Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Extra technical notes from infra/serving side (implementation details):

1) Ingest pipeline placement:
- Best place to apply redaction + trace-id hashing is at the edge aggregator before logs hit our hot-write path; that minimizes any retention of raw values. We will add a sanitization filter stage that operates on configured JSON paths.

2) Trace-ID hashing approach:
- We will implement HMAC-SHA256(tenant_salt, trace_id) and then base64url-encode or hex-truncate to 16 bytes for storage. That keeps determinism and prevents simple reversal.
- Tenant_salt will be stored in KMS and rotated quarterly; rotation will update mapping for new traces only. We will document the rotation implications.

3) Safe-preview mechanics:
- Quarantine bucket: sampled messages routed to a preview API that strips all raw PII and shows pseudonymized trace IDs. Access controlled via RBAC and temporary tokens.

4) Test artifacts we need from PulseCare:
- A small sample of 100 redacted-request logs (you can redact actual PII before sending) so we can validate JSON paths and ensure we don't miss embedded PII in nested objects.
- Confirmation of the list of JSON keys to be redacted (use the attached PIIscope doc as the source of truth).

Deliverables we will produce after alignment:
- Implementation plan (milestones + owner), staging pilot runbook, QA checklist for security review, and cost delta.

I can prepare a short RFC doc once you confirm the keys and trace-id policy.

—Karthik
Infrastructure Engineering Lead
Redwood Inference
